newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamists say no decision on polls, power.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamists say no decision on polls, power.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists said on Thursday no definite decision had been taken to go to early elections or hand over power to Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller in talks between the coalition allies to solve a political crisis.
"At the moment there is no definite result or decision on this issue," Salih Kapusuz, a spokesman for the Islam-based Welfare Party, told Reuters.

Earlier a senior deputy from Ciller's conservative True Path Party said Welfare favoured an early handover of the premiership to her as a way of easing mounting pressure on the coalition from the secularist establishment.
The True Path MP, who declined to be named, said after a key party meeting that elections would be held within a year.
Ciller, the deputy prime minister, has asked Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to make her leader of a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.
Their 11-month-old alliance has been losing deputies in a row with the secularist army over Islamist activism and is close to becoming a minority administration.
